newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields mixed, crown softens further.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields mixed, crown softens further.

text.p: Swedish bond yields remained mixed at midday on Monday with long yields trading at unchanged levels supported by international trends and short yields pushed higher by a weaker crown.
"The crown softening is a reaction to this weekend's news," a trader said.
"That (Finance Minister Erik) Asbrink has said that there currently is no majority within his party for an EMU membership in 1999 is having a negative impact.
"Then we have the statement from Ericsson's chief executive that a possible move abroad is being looked into."
Another trader said fundamentals had nothing to do with the crown softening.
The crown weakened to 4.5710 crowns against the mark from 4.5315 crowns late on Friday and from 4.5640 crowns early on Monday.
The six-month T-bill rate climbed eight basis points to 4.34 percent while the ten-year bond yield was flat at 7.20 percent.
The long yield spread to Germany widened to 137 basis points from 135 as the long end of the market was hampered by higher short yields, dealers said.
